hypothesis_status: UPHELD as a symptom; the refuter's LOCATION was overturned
filed_hypothesis: Address-taken parameter storage may be emitted again as a local symbol.
captain_refutation: a symbol-mapping defect (the address-taken varnode gets its own address-tied local symbol over storage already claimed by an input parameter); look in the P6 variable/scope-restructure plane before P9 emission.
decisions: THE REFUTER'S 'TWO SYMBOLS' READING IS WRONG, MEASURED. There is exactly ONE symbol at the parameter's storage and the `&a0` reference is already bound to it. Instrumented `PrintC::emit_local_var_decls` on the witness: the declared high named `a0` carries `kuna_ref_symbol = Some(SymbolId(10v5))` whose ScopeLocal category is 0 = FUNCTION_PARAMETER. The other declared reference high in the same function (`v7`) carries category -1. So P6 mapped the reference onto the parameter correctly and nothing in the scope-restructure plane needed changing; the defect is entirely in P9 emission.

THE TYPE DISAGREEMENT DOES NOT PROVE TWO SYMBOLS. `unsigned int` in the signature is the FuncProto parameter's type; `int4` in the body is the reference high's own data type. One symbol, two renderers.

ROOT CAUSE: the printer's parameter test is storage-based and an `&parameter` reference has no storage. kuna's `emit_local_var_decls` walks HighVariables (upstream walks the ScopeLocal symbol table for `no_category` symbols) and skips a parameter by asking `containing_category_for_varnode` about each member Varnode. Every Varnode of an `&symbol` reference high is the PTRSUB offset CONSTANT, so nothing is contained by the parameter entry, `is_param` is false, and the high is declared -- under the name it took from the parameter symbol.

FIXED ON SYMBOL IDENTITY, NOT BY RENAMING. The refuter warned that renaming the shadow (`a0_1`) would pass the acceptance while asserting a falsehood. The shipped fix removes the declaration: `references_parameter_symbol` reads the symbol the reference is ALREADY bound to (kuna's `HighVariable::kuna_ref_symbol`, the port of `Varnode::setSymbolReference`) and skips it when its category is FUNCTION_PARAMETER, so `&a0` resolves to the signature's own `a0` and there is one object where the machine has one.

THE JSON HALF WAS FIXED TOO, and it is a separate query. `variable_storage_varrefs` collects a parameter's uses by matching Varnodes against the parameter's storage, which an address-taken parameter has none of; `named_high_varrefs` misses as well because the JSON spells the parameter `param_1` while the high is named `a0`. Added as a THIRD fallback, consulted only when the first two found nothing, so no existing evidence can move. The witness's `param_1` now carries line 18 and addresses 0x401641/0x401650 instead of reading as unused.

REUSED THE EXISTING CONTAINER QUERY. The first draft added a `ScopeLocal::containing_symbol_for_varnode` next to the existing `containing_symbol_for_storage`; they answer the same question, so the new one was dropped. Base-byte containment is also the query `linkSymbol` binds a reference with, so the JSON half resolves exactly the symbol the printer half reads off the reference.

NO STAGE-TEST BLIND SPOT THIS TIME. Unlike the sibling PE needs, the construct reduces to a plain i386 cdecl frame, so `tests/stages/kuna-paramrefdecl.xml` carries it as a bytechunk and the two-pass form works. The vendored fixture exists only because `tests/cli` probes need a real binary and the acceptance's target is a dataset file.
